ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle A=90^\circ$, BD bisects $\angle ABC$ and intersects AC at point D, AB=4, BC=12, and AD=3. If point P moves on BC, when DP is minimized, what is the area of $\triangle CDP$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Since $\angle A=90^\circ$, \\
it follows that BD=$\sqrt{AB^{2}+AD^{2}}=\sqrt{4^{2}+3^{2}}=5$, \\
When DP is at its minimum, DP=3, and DP$\perp$BC, \\
thus $\angle$DPB=$\angle$DPC=$90^\circ$, \\
so PB=$\sqrt{BD^{2}-DP^{2}}=\sqrt{5^{2}-3^{2}}=4$, \\
thus CP=BC-PB=12-4=8, \\
therefore, the area of $\triangle CDP$=$\frac{1}{2}$CP$\times$DP=$\frac{1}{2}\times8\times3=\boxed{12}$, \\
i.e., when DP is at its minimum, the area of $\triangle CDP$ is \boxed{12}.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, the vertex A of triangle ABC is above, B is on the left, and C is at the lower right; there is a right-angle mark at A, indicating that AB and AC are perpendicular. Point D is located on side AC, and line segment BD connects from B to D. Point P is located on side BC, and line segment DP connects from D to P. Reasoning: Because A in the figure is a right angle, and D is on AC, AD is perpendicular to AB, and AD is exactly the perpendicular distance from point D to side AB, AD=3. Also because the problem statement gives that BD bisects angle ABC, points on an angle bisector have equal distances to the two sides of the angle, so the perpendicular distance from point D to side BC is also 3. Thus the area of triangle CDP is (1/2)*CP*DP=(1/2)*8*3=12.
